## IndexSelectorReference interface

One object denoted by its zero-based position within its container, bound to the client that decoded it: what an output position holds whose target has no identifier and is found by its position within its parent.

**Signature:**

```typescript
interface IndexSelectorReference<T, R extends string = string> extends SelectorReference<T, R>
```

**Extends:** [SelectorReference](./contracts.selectorreference.md)<!-- -->&lt;T, R&gt;

## Remarks

A [SelectorReference](./contracts.selectorreference.md) whose selector is always an [IndexSelector](./contracts.indexselector.md) and whose container is always present, as an identity reference to the object the field was read through. Every container level is in identity form, so a position never appears inside a container. It is assignable to [ObjectReference](./contracts.objectreference.md) and to [ObjectReferenceVariant](./contracts.objectreferencevariant.md)<!-- -->, so generic hydration accepts it, while a typed caller can see that it is positional.

The reference means whatever object holds that position when it is resolved, not the object observed when it was read: it drifts as objects are added to, removed from or moved within the container. An index past the end fails to resolve with an invalid-selection error, and a container that no longer exists with a target-not-found error.
